step.label: Två händer, ett kort till platsen

prompt.text: Locked camera, one continuous shot. A practised card dealer deals one card with both hands at work. Her hand at the shoe strokes the yellow card out of the window and takes it by its edges between thumb and fingers. She carries it low over the felt the short way to its place in front of the shoe, at the lower right of the picture, where the last frame shows it. On the way her wrist turns over and the card turns with it in her fingers, from its yellow back to its blue face: the card never turns by itself and never leaves her fingers before it lies. She lays it flat at its place and lets go. While she does this her other hand does not lie still: it lifts a little from the table and opens toward the card's place in a small, easy presenting gesture as the card comes down, then settles back flat on the table in front of her, as in the last frame. The hand that dealt goes back to the shoe and rests on it, as in the last frame. Her eyes follow the card. She moves naturally, with soft, relaxed arms and wrists. Only one card moves: a small card, about half as long as her hand, which keeps the size it has in the last frame all the way from the shoe to its place. Its back is plain solid yellow and its face is solid blue with a small pink cross in the middle and a small red dot in one corner, as the last frame shows it. A yellow card shows in the window of the shoe all the time: as she strokes one out, the next one is already there.
